note: Match the look targets. Each target is a hidden setup; its numbers are measured from it when the student opens it, so they always match the target picture. Scoring compares measured properties, never pixels. Drafts until Tom approves.

items.title: Mysterious album cover
items.brief: A musician wants a dark, mysterious cover: one side of the face in deep shadow, background nearly black.

shadowStops.ifTooLow: The shadow side is lighter than the target. What could you turn down, turn off, or move?
shadowStops.ifTooHigh: The shadow side is even darker than the target. What could add just a little light?

backdropMean.ifTooLow: The backdrop is darker than the target. Is anything lighting it?
backdropMean.ifTooHigh: The backdrop is brighter than the target. How could you keep light off it?

keySide.ifWrong: The light comes from the other side in the target. Where should the key go?

hints: The target uses only one light.
The key is far to the side, almost 90°.
Look at the backdrop: very dark.

careerConnection.title: Album cover photographer
careerConnection.text: Music photographers light for mood first. A low-key cover can say more about a sound than the musician's face does. Art directors often ask for exactly this look, and you have to deliver it on set, fast.

items.title: Bright yearbook portrait
items.brief: School portraits need a bright, friendly look: soft even light and a white background.

shadowStops.ifTooHigh: The shadows are deeper than the target. What could lift them?

backdropMean.ifTooLow: The backdrop is darker than the target. How do you make white paper look white?

overallMean.ifTooLow: The whole picture is darker than the target. Is the camera exposing for a bright, high-key look?
overallMean.ifTooHigh: The picture is brighter than the target. What could you bring down?

hints: Two big, soft lights at the front.
The backdrop has its own light.

careerConnection.title: School and event photographer
careerConnection.text: School photographers set up one look and repeat it for hundreds of students in a day, so the setup has to be even, flattering, and quick to check.

items.title: Actor's headshot
items.brief: An actor needs a classic headshot: clear key side, gentle fill, and a rim light so they stand out from a grey background.

shadowStops.ifTooLow: The shadows are lighter than the target. Is the fill too strong?
shadowStops.ifTooHigh: The shadow side is darker than the target. What could you add or raise?

backdropMean.ifTooLow: The backdrop is darker than the target. How far back is it?
backdropMean.ifTooHigh: The backdrop is brighter than the target. How far back is it, and what's lighting it?

rimScore.ifTooLow: The target has a rim of light around the head. Which light makes that?
rimScore.ifTooHigh: The rim is stronger than in the target.

keySide.ifWrong: The key is on the other side in the target.

hints: Three lights: key, fill and back.
The key is about 45° camera-left and above the face.
The backdrop is white paper, quite far back.

careerConnection.title: Headshot photographer
careerConnection.text: Casting directors look at hundreds of headshots, so actors need a clear, honest, well-lit picture. Headshot photographers often shoot three-point setups all day and adjust the fill to each face.

items.title: Film noir detective
items.brief: A 1940s-style crime poster: hard light from the camera's right side, deep shadows, dark background.

shadowStops.ifTooLow: The shadows are softer and lighter than the target. What makes shadows deep and hard?
shadowStops.ifTooHigh: The shadows are even deeper than the target.

backdropMean.ifTooHigh: The background should be nearly black. What's lighting it?

keySide.ifWrong: In the target the light comes from the camera's right.

hints: It's on the camera-right side this time.
A Fresnel close to spot gives hard light.

careerConnection.title: Cinematographer (director of photography)
careerConnection.text: Cinematographers design the lighting for every shot of a film. Film noir is a style built almost entirely from hard, low-key light, and it's still copied in crime dramas and music videos.

items.title: Warm documentary interview
items.brief: A documentary wants a warm, cosy interview look: the face glowing a little orange, soft shadows.

colorCast.ifTooLow: The target looks warmer (more orange). What controls how warm a light is?
colorCast.ifTooHigh: Your picture is warmer than the target.

shadowStops.ifTooHigh: The shadow side is darker than the target. What could lift it?

hints: The lights are set warm, around 3200 K.
The camera's white balance is still Daylight.

careerConnection.title: Gaffer
careerConnection.text: The gaffer is the head of the lighting crew on a film or documentary. They choose the lights, gels and colour temperatures that make the look the director wants.
